narration: You got the raise, bought the car, upgraded the apartment — and still feel like you're barely keeping up. Your brain was actually built this way.
visual: Three icons spring in one by one: dollar sign (raise), SVG car (new car), SVG house (upgraded home) — each with a checkmark. Then a red 'AND STILL FEEL BROKE' text slams in.

narration: Scientists call it the hedonic treadmill. Every upgrade you make, your brain resets what 'normal' feels like within about one year. You end up right back at baseline.
visual: Animated SVG treadmill — belt moves continuously but the running person stays in place. Label 'HEDONIC TREADMILL'. Then '1 YEAR LATER... BACK TO BASELINE' fades in red.

narration: Here's what's wild — surveys show people always think they need 40% more than they earn to feel comfortable. Earn $50K, you want $70K. Earn $200K, you want $280K.
visual: Animated bar chart: three income levels side by side — blue bar for 'HAVE', red bar 40% taller for 'WANT'. Labels $50K/$70K, $100K/$140K, $200K/$280K. Gap stays constant.

narration: A Wharton study tracked 33,000 adults. Happiness does rise with income — but above $500,000, earning more barely moves the needle at all.
visual: Axes graph with a logarithmic happiness curve drawn in real-time. Income on x-axis. Red dashed vertical line at $500K+ with label 'GAINS NEAR ZERO'.

narration: Scientists call this arrival fallacy — the belief that happiness is waiting at the next income milestone. The finish line keeps moving no matter how fast you run.
visual: Person runs right across screen but a checkered finish line retreats faster. Overhead labels cycle: 'EARN $50K' → 'EARN $100K' → 'EARN $200K'. Person never reaches it.

narration: The fix isn't earning less. Research shows spending on experiences — not upgrades — actually breaks the treadmill. Set a written 'enough' number. Follow for more money psychology.
visual: Three checklist items slide in: 'Buy EXPERIENCES not things', 'Write down your enough number', 'Compare to past you — not neighbors'. Then blue CTA button: FOLLOW FOR MORE.
